THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio.
β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the
gradient of y with respect to each uncertain input x_k, computed by
the compiler at emit-time via forward-mode automatic differentiation.

Sounio — a language originally designed for epistemic typed computing —
into an automatic-differentiation language.

compiler's sensitivity as the gradient. No external library. No manual
derivative. The compiler knows dL/dx because it computed it while
emitting the code.

Expected: x → 3.0, L → 0.

comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural).
Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/
multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT
union topology across user-defined function calls — the return
inherited only the *last* argument's channel set.
Concretely, for
fn my_sum(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a + b }
let x = k0.value   // channel 0
let y = k1.value   // channel 1
hessian_of(my_sum(x, y), 0, 1)

H_{0,1} was REFUSED at type-check because channel 0 was not in the set.
Week-3 unions the channel sets of every argument into the return
topology (conservative upper bound, matching the atan2/pow discipline).
The same program now type-checks.  The runtime value is 0.0 because
inter-procedural SSHADOW propagation is not yet wired — topology
tracking and shadow tracking are orthogonal concerns.  This test
asserts that the type checker accepts the query; the shadow pipeline
is covered by epistemic_hessian_*.

    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn emit_u64(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 4) as usize] = ((v >> 32) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 5) as usize] = ((v >> 40) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 6) as usize] = ((v >> 48) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 7) as usize] = ((v >> 56) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Build code: print_f64 at offset 0, then main stub
    var code = code_buffer_new()
    code = ast_emit_print_f64_builtin(code)
    let main_off = code.len
    code = emit_main(code, 0)  // print_f64 is at code offset 0

    let code_size = code.len
    let vaddr_base: i64 = 0x400000
    let code_file_off: i64 = 0x80  // After ELF header (64 bytes) + 1 program header (56 bytes) = 120 = 0x78, round up
    let entry_vaddr = vaddr_base + code_file_off + main_off

    // Build minimal ELF64 header
    var elf: [i8; 4096] = [0; 4096]

    // ELF magic: 7f 45 4c 46
    elf[0 as usize] = 0x7f as i8
    elf[1 as usize] = 0x45 as i8  // E
    elf[2 as usize] = 0x4c as i8  // L
    elf[3 as usize] = 0x46 as i8  // F

    // EI_CLASS=2 (64-bit), EI_DATA=1 (LE), EI_VERSION=1, EI_OSABI=0
    elf[4 as usize] = 2 as i8
    elf[5 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[6 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[7 as usize] = 0 as i8

    // e_type=2 (ET_EXEC), e_machine=0x3E (x86-64)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 16, 2)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 18, 0x3E)
    // e_version=1
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 20, 1)
    // e_entry
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 24, entry_vaddr)
    // e_phoff = 64 (right after ELF header)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 32, 64)
    // e_shoff = 0 (no section headers)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 40, 0)
    // e_flags = 0
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 48, 0)
    // e_ehsize = 64
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 52, 64)
    // e_phentsize = 56
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 54, 56)
    // e_phnum = 1
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 56, 1)
    // e_shentsize = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 58, 0)
    // e_shnum = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 60, 0)
    // e_shstrndx = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 62, 0)

    // Program header (LOAD) at offset 64
    // p_type = 1 (PT_LOAD)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 64, 1)
    // p_flags = 5 (PF_R | PF_X)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 68, 5)
    // p_offset = 0
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 72, 0)
    // p_vaddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 80, vaddr_base)
    // p_paddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 88, vaddr_base)
    // p_filesz = code_file_off + code_size
    let total_file = code_file_off + code_size
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 96, total_file)
    // p_memsz = total_file
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 104, total_file)
    // p_align = 0x1000
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 112, 0x1000)

    // Copy code bytes into ELF at code_file_off
    var ci: i64 = 0
    while ci < code_size {
        elf[(code_file_off + ci) as usize] = code.bytes[ci as usize]
        ci = ci + 1
    }

    let elf_size = code_file_off + code_size

    // Write ELF to file using VM builtin
    let wr = write_file("/tmp/sprint235_f64.elf", elf, elf_size)
    if wr < 0 {
        print("FAIL: could not write ELF\n")
        return 1
    }

    print("PASS: ELF written size=")
    print_int(elf_size)
    print(" entry=0x")
    print_int(entry_vaddr)
    print(" code=")
    print_int(code_size)
    print("\n")
    0
}
